identification: YahooFundamentals stock-data project repackaged with obfuscated Windows LuaJIT loaders
basis: The README promotes unrelated Windows Lua payloads as the stock-data application. Configuration-gated code requests elevated Defender exclusions for the whole system drive and executable extensions, installs durable execution, and processes remotely supplied file tasks. These effects do not serve financial-data retrieval. Public-registry provenance does not outweigh the recovered code.

targets.role: Source distribution and misleading download lure
Scanner-recovered layer of the same Lua loader

review: Read RULES.md and TAXONOMY.md. Inspected every outer and nested member. The Python program reads ticker symbols, obtains Yahoo Finance fundamentals, computes ratios, and writes CSV; it is plausible stock-data software. It is not what the advertised Windows bundles launch.

Fundamentals-Yahoo-v2.3.zip contains Launcher.cmd (start util.exe lj_asm.txt), util.exe and lj_asm.txt. YahooFundamentals-v1.3.zip contains Launcher.cmd (start luajit.exe crt.txt), luajit.exe, lua51.dll and crt.txt. PE imports, LuaJIT CLI/runtime data and native main disassembly identify the interpreter carrier; its name or ordinary runtime APIs are not treated as malware identity.

Ran atomscan in slow mode with updates disabled and cleave facts on the distribution, both nested archives, both Lua scripts and all three PE files. Checked decoded literals and contextual matches separately from raw source.

Independently normalized arithmetic and indexed string reassembly using a Lua grammar. For crt.txt, executed only the constant-table prefix to reverse its permutations and custom radix-64 alphabet (1069 entries), then substituted 1271 table reads. The current script uses decimal escapes, indexed fragment shuffles, encrypted strings, environment indirection, and a flattened numeric dispatcher.

A restricted Lua 5.1 interpreter with no host I/O, networking, Python builtins or native FFI and a bounded instruction budget exposed the string-decryption closure. Static block-local analysis supplied ciphertext/seed arguments to that closure: 996 constants recovered for lj_asm.txt and 975 for crt.txt. Followed decoded assignments, function aliases, state transitions and call arguments rather than judging strings alone.

Both scripts request ffi and bit, declare Win32 types, attempt to load lua51.dll, query the console window and hide it. In the modeled x64 branch they allocate VirtualAlloc(nil,10,12288,64) and construct 65 48 8b 04 25 60 00 00 00 c3 (read GS:[0x60], return). A separate x86 run of lj_asm.txt, matching the 32-bit util.exe carrier, requests seven bytes and constructs 64 a1 30 00 00 00 c3 (read FS:[0x30], return). These are local PEB readers. Subsequent source traverses the loader list and export directories to resolve APIs. These small buffers are not evidence of cross-process injection or acquired-payload activation.

Further mocked import resolution exposed initialization of WinExec, file, WinInet, registry, token-query and randomness APIs. The controlled trace reached GET ip-api.com/json/, JSON-to-Lua compilation and a connectivity check to microsoft.com. All OS/network effects were mocked; canned responses used to advance the trace are not deployment evidence.

In decoded current-source control flow, loader.bypass_defender == 1 selects dispatcher state 5170423, which builds powershell Start-Process with comment-split arguments, -Verb RunAs, hidden-window options, and Add-MpPreference -ExclusionPath $env:SystemDrive -ExclusionExtension .exe, .dll -Force, then passes the resulting command and show flag zero to the resolved command wrapper. RunAs requests elevation; successful elevation or a UAC bypass is not established.

loader.autorun gates persistence. The source formats schtasks /create /sc daily /st %02d:%02d /f with randomized hours 10..14 and minutes 0..59, appends a task name and action, and invokes the command wrapper. Other source constructs a one-shot Register-ScheduledTask command and accesses Run/StartupApproved registry locations. Actual changes depend on configuration and permissions.

Current defaults include http://89.169.12.246 and four Polygon RPC providers; the older bundle includes http://178.17.59.88 and polygon-rpc.com. The current eth_call body uses contract 0x1823A9a0Ec8e0C25dD957D0841e3D41a4474bAdc and selector 0x3bc5de30. These are evidence locations, not signature gates. No live server, contract or next-stage payload was fetched.

Task dispatch reads tasks, file_path, file_name and start, with executable, rundll32/DLL, cmd/batch, PowerShell and Lua dispatch branches. HTTP helpers construct POST /api/ requests and multipart bodies. GDI helpers assemble bitmap pixels with GetDC, CreateDIBSection and BitBlt. Retained neutral API/format traits do not assert that those pixels were exfiltrated or that any particular remote task actually ran.

The independently recovered source also converts hexadecimal text with an aliased tonumber(...,16) and performs byte-XOR transforms. Added coverage for the verified radix conversion without inferring an encryption direction or a data-transfer relationship.
missing_context: Whether any user launched a bundled batch file
The remote configuration, including autorun and bypass_defender settings, at deployment time
Remote task responses, downloaded payloads, successful persistence/elevation, or present ownership/activity of the endpoints

changes.reason: Source-literal shape is not obfuscation or a code metric. Changed suspicious to notable and required an actual radix-64 alphabet; the old dot patterns crossed quotes and matched unrelated strings. Preserved Lua/platform scope.
Preserved matcher and Windows batch/PowerShell scope; ordinary Lua arguments establish no deception. Notable argument observation.
Retired redundant compound observation; existing notable START capability already covers its required launch. No alias added to the full command-mode leaf.
Retired unsupported hostile co-occurrence. Existing Polygon-client, RWX-allocation and PEB-cast atoms remain. The local PEB-reader stub does not prove acquired-payload activation or T1055.

Consolidated related archive/doc claims as a lure and explicitly required Defender-bypass content. Description states co-occurrence, not a proved URL-to-member link, supply-chain replacement, or linked execution.

New notable structured detection binds an aliased tonumber member to radix-16 invocation; covers both recovered literals and the explicit selector/radix register form. No sample-specific names, addresses or seeds.

placement_and_reference_audit: All destinations are existing admitted leaves. Audited exact IDs and ancestor/directory selectors. No external exact YAML consumers of the retired rules existed; the removed launch compound referenced its old atom internally. Neutral table and argument observations intentionally leave intent selectors; those selectors are not broadened to reintroduce the false claim. Existing source rules outside the selected IDs remain unchanged. Historical scan records retain historical IDs. New metadata and argument facts cannot feed an objective by an illegal dependency; no new selector is used as multiple evidence roles. New lure requires three distinct roles and uses existing named observations rather than copied matchers.

controls.checks: Positive alias forms, wrong radix/member/callee, overwritten bindings, padded literal tables versus prose/short strings, ordinary Lua text-file launch, and image/page ZIP wording without a payload. Documentation alone produces no hostile finding.

scan_notes: Atomscan emits model feature-spec compatibility warnings and exits 1 for the malicious result. Verdict is based on reverse engineering. Final make validate is required separately.
